cf.title: Wrong result for whole-row IS NOT NULL with dropped columns

input.subject: Wrong result for whole-row IS NOT NULL with dropped columns

verdict_reasoning: The proposal fixes a reproducible wrong result by making plan-time folding match ExecEvalRowNullInt(), and no objection survived at levels 1a or 1b. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is a fixable level 2 point: indexes and stored values built under the old folding keep the old result after a minor update. A committer who knows the planner still has to sign the back-patch to six branches, two of them untested.

brief.title: Skip dropped columns when the planner folds ROW(...) IS [NOT] NULL
brief.problem: The planner folds ROW(...)::type IS NOT NULL to constant false when the named rowtype has a dropped column, because it treats the dropped-column placeholder as a null field. Users get wrong results: a WHERE clause silently drops every row, and a whole-row CHECK constraint cannot be added or satisfied. Virtual generated columns expose it most easily, but casts to a named rowtype hit it on all supported branches.
brief.proposed_design: When eval_const_expressions() simplifies a NullTest on a RowExpr of a named composite type, it looks up the rowtype's tuple descriptor and skips fields for dropped attributes. This matches ExecEvalRowNullInt() in the executor. Back-branch versions down to 14 use the same approach, with small API differences.
author_claims: Plan-time and execution-time results differ today; the fix makes the planner match the executor.
The ROW(...)::type case exists on PG 14 and later, so all supported branches need the fix.
With the patch, EXPLAIN shows per-field tests such as ((a IS NOT NULL) AND (b IS NOT NULL)) instead of false.
Checking attisdropped in the tuple descriptor also covers stored views whose RowExpr still holds a Var for the dropped attribute.
brief.thread_state: Two reviewers, Sho Ito and Joao Rito, report no remaining code concerns; Rito tested v2 on master, REL_18, REL_17 and REL_14. No committer has replied, and the REL_15 and REL_16 patches are untested.
unclear: The material does not show measured planning-time cost of the tuple descriptor lookup per NullTest.
No one confirms whether other planner simplifications on RowExpr, such as predicate proof or IS NULL folding elsewhere, have the same dropped-column flaw.
The thread does not say whether the stored view case needs other fixes, such as rewriting stored rules after DROP ATTRIBUTE.

objections.title: Back-patched fix leaves expression and partial indexes built under old folding
objections.failure_scenario: A user on REL_16 has a partial index with predicate `ROW(a, b)::ts IS NOT NULL` on a table with a dropped column. Before the fix the predicate folded to false, so the index holds no rows and the planner never chose it. After the minor update the planner proves the predicate and uses the empty index, so queries silently miss every pre-existing row.
objections.argument: Index expressions, index predicates and stored generated columns go through eval_const_expressions() when values are computed, so values written before the fix carry the old false result. The patch changes the folded result on all branches down to 14, but the thread and commit messages do not say what happens to data already derived from that folding. The same applies to an expression index on such a test, where old entries hold false. Back-patched planner fixes of this kind usually come with release-note advice to REINDEX affected indexes, and the proposal does not yet say that.
objections.author_must_show: Which stored objects (expression indexes, partial indexes, stored generated columns) can hold values computed by the old folding, and what release-note advice tells users to rebuild them?

critic.reasoning: Postgres runs index predicates, index expressions and stored generated column expressions through eval_const_expressions() at build and insert time, so old entries reflect the wrong folding. The thread and commit messages do not mention REINDEX advice; the case is narrow and needs only a release-note line.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent ALTER TABLE DROP NOT NULL on child tables if parent column has it
precedents_retrieved.summary: Prevent ALTER TABLE ... DROP NOT NULL on a child table when the same column in a parent table is marked NOT NULL, so that the constraint can only be dropped from the parent. The patch added a function in pg_inherits.c to list a relation's parents and a new index on pg_inherits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the approach was wrong because it does not help decide whether to propagate DROP NOT NULL from a parent to its children, and pointed to the earlier plan of storing NOT NULL constraints in pg_constraint with inheritance counts as CHECK constraints do. After Vitaly Burovoy reported that he was writing such a patch, which already forbids dropping inherited NOT NULLs, the author withdrew his proposal in favour of that work.

precedents_retrieved.title: GUC-ify WALSender's MAX_SEND_SIZE constant
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch turns the walsender constant MAX_SEND_SIZE (128kB) into a GUC, wal_sender_max_send_size, capped at wal_segment_size. The aim was larger WAL reads per walsender iteration on storage with high latency and high bandwidth, such as Ceph RBD volumes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the GUC is one more setting nobody can realistically tune, and that it is a poor proxy for the real issue: read size against high-latency storage, better solved by read_stream support for reading WAL. Jakub Wartak agreed and asked for a reproducible benchmark. The author had left the company and could not provide numbers, so Michael Paquier marked the patch rejected.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner fold IS NULL and IS NOT NULL checks on primary key columns, and later also on NOT NULL constraint columns, into constants at planning time. It does this only when the column is not on the nullable side of an outer join.

precedents_retrieved.summary: Andres Freund proposed a prototype patch series to speed up expression evaluation, interpreted and JIT-compiled, and to make JITed code cacheable. roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P8] also touches NULL folding in eval_const_expressions, but it added new folding based on NOT NULL constraints, while this patch removes a wrong fold so the planner matches ExecEvalRowNullInt(). Its key sentence, about waiting for better infrastructure before adding new NULL smarts, does not apply to a wrong-result fix. The thread cites no earlier discussion of this bug.

Apart from the stored-data question, the change makes plan-time folding match the executor and the SQL meaning of a row without dropped attributes. It adds no syntax, GUC, catalog or pg_dump surface. [P8] concerns adding new NULL folding and does not apply to fixing existing folding.

The proposal changes only plan-time folding in clauses.c, with no change to on-disk format, WAL, catalogs, wire protocol or exported structs, so pg_upgrade, standbys and back-branch ABI are unaffected. Stored views and CHECK constraints keep their stored trees and are re-planned with the fixed logic after a minor update.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes how the planner folds a NullTest so the result matches what ExecEvalRowNullInt() already returns. It adds no user surface, privilege, catalog access or resource use that a user controls. The fix makes an RLS policy or security barrier view that uses ROW(...) IS NOT NULL give the result the executor already defines, so it opens no new access path.

This is a wrong-result fix that brings the planner in line with ExecEvalRowNullInt(), so it adds no new mechanism to maintain. [P8] does not apply: its rejected design opened the table in eval_const_expressions(), and this patch reads the rowtype's tuple descriptor, which costs only planning of NullTests on named RowExprs. No committer has replied yet, and the REL_15 and REL_16 patches are untested. Those points affect committability, not the merits.

This is a wrong-result bug fix in eval_const_expressions(), so no existing feature, extension or hook can replace it. Users can only avoid the folding by rewriting queries, and they cannot do that for a whole-row CHECK constraint on a table with virtual generated columns. [P8] concerns adding new NULL folding, and its recorded reason does not apply to removing incorrect folding.

This is a wrong-result bug fix with no new user-visible surface, so the demand test does not apply in the usual way. The thread shows reproducible silent row loss in WHERE clauses and CHECK constraints that can never be satisfied, reached through casts to named rowtypes on all supported branches. Correct query results are needed by every user who hits the case, and the cost falls only on the planner's handling of NullTest on named-type RowExprs. [P8] is about adding new NULL-folding smarts, not about fixing an existing incorrect fold, so it does not apply.
